title: Acute Retrosternal Chest Pain
learning_objectives: Perform targeted OPQRST history for acute chest pain
Screen for high-risk red flags including radiation and autonomic signs
Identify acute myocardial infarction on STAT 12-lead ECG
Initiate immediate dual antiplatelet therapy and emergent catheterization activation

patient.name: Robert Chen
patient.opening_statement: Doctor, please... It feels like an elephant is sitting right in the middle of my chest. I started feeling dizzy and breaking out in a cold sweat on my way into the office.
patient.initial_statement: Doctor, please... It feels like an elephant is sitting right in the middle of my chest. I started feeling dizzy and breaking out in a cold sweat on my way into the office.
patient.presentation_complaint: Severe pressure and heaviness in my chest that started less than an hour ago.

chief_complaint.value: I started having this really heavy pressure in my chest.

onset_activity.value: I was walking up two flights of stairs to my office.

location.value: Right in the middle of my chest.

character.value: It feels like a deep, heavy crushing pressure, like someone is squeezing my chest in a vice.

severity.value: About an 8 out of 10 right now.

radiation.value: Yes, it goes into my left jaw and down my left arm.

aggravating_factors.value: Moving around or minimal exertion makes it noticeably worse.

relieving_factors.value: Nothing really makes it better. Even stopping and resting in my chair did not relieve it at all.

pertinent_negatives: No pleuritic sharp pain on deep inspiration
No tearing pain between shoulder blades

family_history: Father had a fatal heart attack at age 52; Mother has type 2 diabetes.
social_history: Smokes 0.5 packs per day for 25 years. Drinks 1-2 glasses of wine on weekends. No illicit substances.

examination.name: Cardiovascular Examination & Auscultation
examination.findingDescription: Regular tachycardia at 98 bpm. S1/S2 present. Soft S4 gallop audible at apex. JVP 3 cm above sternal angle at 45 degrees. Peripheral pulses equal bilaterally.
examination.clinicalSignificance: S4 gallop indicates reduced LV compliance from acute myocardial ischemia.

examination.name: Pulmonary Auscultation & Chest Wall Palpation
examination.findingDescription: Clear breath sounds bilaterally. No wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi. No chest wall tenderness to palpation.
examination.clinicalSignificance: Absence of chest wall tenderness rules out costochondritis; clear lungs exclude acute pulmonary edema.

examination.name: General Appearance & Diaphoresis
examination.findingDescription: Cool, clammy extremities with marked forehead and palmar diaphoresis. Capillary refill 2.5 seconds.
examination.clinicalSignificance: Intense autonomic sympathetic discharge in acute coronary syndrome.

examination.name: Abdominal Examination
examination.findingDescription: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. No guarding, rebound, or palpable pulsatile mass.

investigations.name: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (STAT)
investigations.result: ST Elevation in II, III, aVF (Inferior STEMI)
investigations.interpretation: Sinus rhythm at 96 bpm. 2.5 mm ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF with reciprocal ST depression in leads I and aVL.

investigations.name: Portable Chest Radiograph (CXR)
investigations.result: Normal cardiothoracic ratio, clear fields, no mediastinal widening

immediate_actions: Activate Cardiac Catheterization Lab for Emergent Primary PCI
Initiate IV Unfractionated Heparin bolus and infusion
Provide sublingual nitroglycerin (if systolic BP > 100 mmHg and no RV infarction)

high_value_questions: Radiation to jaw or left arm
Past medical history and cardiac risk factors

title: Acute Severe Dyspnea & Wheezing
learning_objectives: Screen for respiratory muscle fatigue and accessory muscle use
Administer back-to-back inhaled bronchodilators and systemic corticosteroids

patient.name: Elena Rostova
patient.opening_statement: Doctor... I can't... breathe... Used my blue inhaler... four times... still tight...
patient.initial_statement: Doctor... I can't... breathe... Used my blue inhaler... four times... still tight...
patient.presentation_complaint: I can barely catch my breath... My inhaler isn't working.

chief_complaint.value: I started having severe trouble catching my breath, and my blue inhaler isn't working.

onset_activity.value: I was visiting a friend who has two cats.

character.value: It feels like breathing through a thin straw, with a tight band squeezing my chest.

severity.value: It's about an 8 out of 10 difficulty breathing.

radiation.value: No, it stays right where it is. It hasn't spread anywhere else.

timing.value: It hasn't really gone away and has gotten worse.

aggravating_factors.value: Any physical activity or breathing in cold air makes it much worse.

relieving_factors.value: My inhaler gave only about ten minutes of slight relief before the tightness came right back.

pertinent_negatives: No fever, chills, or purulent sputum
No leg swelling or prior DVT

past_medical_history: Moderate persistent asthma diagnosed at age 11
Cat dander and grass pollen allergy
One prior ICU admission for asthma at age 19
medications: Albuterol 90 mcg HFA inhaler as needed
family_history: Mother has asthma; Brother had severe eczema growing up.
social_history: Never smoked, denies vaping or illicit substances.

examination.name: Pulmonary Auscultation & Work of Breathing
examination.findingDescription: Markedly prolonged expiratory phase. High-pitched polyphonic expiratory wheezes throughout all lung fields. Supraclavicular and intercostal retractions present.
examination.clinicalSignificance: Severe diffuse bronchospasm with significant airflow limitation.

examination.name: Precordial Auscultation
examination.findingDescription: Tachycardic regular rhythm at 112 bpm. Normal S1/S2. No murmurs or gallops.
examination.clinicalSignificance: Sinus tachycardia secondary to respiratory distress and albuterol use.

investigations.name: Chest Radiograph (CXR)
investigations.result: Hyperinflation with flattened diaphragms; no focal consolidation or pneumothorax
investigations.interpretation: Hyperinflation consistent with acute air trapping.

immediate_actions: Inhaled Albuterol + Ipratropium bromide nebulization back-to-back x 3
Oral Prednisone 60 mg or IV Methylprednisolone 60 mg STAT
contraindicated_actions: Sedatives or anxiolytics (risk of respiratory depression)

red_flags: Inability to speak in full sentences
critical_actions: Deliver nebulized short-acting beta agonist + anticholinergic

title: Migratory Right Lower Quadrant Abdominal Pain
learning_objectives: Trace classic visceral-to-somatic pain migration in acute abdomen
Elicit peritoneal signs (McBurney tenderness, Rovsing, Psoas sign)
Order targeted abdominal ultrasound/CT imaging and inflammatory labs
Keep patient NPO and obtain urgent surgical consultation

patient.name: Marcus Vance
patient.opening_statement: Doc, every bump in the road on the way here was pure agony. It started near my navel but now it's focused low down on the right side.
patient.initial_statement: Doc, every bump in the road on the way here was pure agony. It started near my navel but now it's focused low down on the right side.
patient.presentation_complaint: My stomach started hurting around my belly button yesterday, but now it has moved down to the right side and hurts when I walk.

chief_complaint.value: My stomach started hurting around my belly button yesterday, and now it has moved down to my lower right side.

onset_timing.value: It started yesterday evening, around 7 PM.

onset_activity.value: I was just relaxing at home yesterday evening.

location.value: Low down on the right side of my stomach.

character.value: It started as a dull ache around my navel, but now it's a sharp, constant pain low down on my right side.

radiation.value: It moved from around my belly button down to the lower right side of my stomach.

timing.value: Yes, it hasn't really gone away.

aggravating_factors.value: Coughing, walking, or any bumps make the pain much sharper.

relieving_factors.value: Lying completely still helps a little, but nothing really takes the pain away.

pertinent_negatives: No dysuria, hematuria, or flank pain

medications: None. Took 500 mg acetaminophen 3 hours ago with no relief
family_history: No significant medical issues in immediate family.
social_history: Non-smoker, drinks socially on weekends, no illicit substances.

examination.name: Focused Abdominal Palpation & Peritoneal Maneuvers
examination.findingDescription: Marked focal tenderness at McBurney's point with involuntary guarding. Positive Rovsing sign (RLQ pain on LLQ palpation). Positive Psoas sign on passive right hip extension.
examination.clinicalSignificance: Classic peritoneal signs of acute localized appendicitis.

examination.name: General Physical Appearance
examination.findingDescription: Patient lies still with right hip slightly flexed to reduce peritoneal tension. Mild low-grade flushing.

investigations.name: Abdominal Ultrasound (Right Lower Quadrant)
investigations.result: Non-compressible, blind-ending tubular structure measuring 8.2 mm in diameter with periappendiceal fluid
investigations.interpretation: Sonographic evidence of acute non-perforated appendicitis.

investigations.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC with differential)
investigations.result: WBC 14.8 x10^9/L (Leukocytosis with 84% neutrophils / left shift)
investigations.interpretation: Elevated white cell count indicating acute inflammatory response.

immediate_actions: Keep patient NPO (Nil Per Os) immediately
Request Urgent General Surgery Consultation for Appendectomy
Initiate IV fluid resuscitation (Normal Saline or Ringer's Lactate)
Administer broad-spectrum perioperative IV Antibiotics (Ceftriaxone + Metronidazole)
contraindicated_actions: Cathartics or enemas (risk of appendiceal perforation)

high_value_questions: Pain migration from periumbilical to RLQ
critical_actions: Elicit McBurney's point tenderness and Rovsing/Psoas sign
Order ultrasound or CT abdomen and CBC
